paragraphs.title: Noah and His Sons Are Blessed, and Life Begins in the New World

easy.question: Whom did God bless at the beginning of these verses?
answers: Noah and his sons
The beasts of the earth
The fish of the sea
easy.explanation: The first verse says, “And God blessed Noah and his sons.”

easy.question: What did God command Noah and his sons to do?
answers: Build an ark
Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth
Hide from the animals
easy.explanation: God commanded them to be fruitful, multiply, and replenish the earth.

easy.question: What was given to human beings as food according to verse 3?
answers: Only grass
Only fish
Every living moving thing
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you.”

medium.question: According to verse 2, what would happen because of humanity’s position among the animals?
answers: The animals would fear human beings
Human beings would fear every animal
The animals would cease to live
medium.explanation: The verse says that the fear and dread of human beings would be upon the animals, birds, creeping things, and fish.

medium.question: In the phrase “the fear of you and the dread of you,” what does “fear” mean?
answers: Your joy
The fear or awe that you inspire
Your location
medium.explanation: The context describes animals fearing human beings, so “fear” refers to the fear or awe they feel toward people.

medium.question: What is the order of ideas in verses 1–3?
answers: Eating animals, fear, then blessing
Fear of humans, filling the earth, then building the ark
Blessing and multiplying, animals’ fear, then permission to eat animals
medium.explanation: First God blesses them and commands them to multiply; then the animals’ fear is described; finally, permission to eat living creatures is given.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the word “every” in the phrase “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you”?
answers: The permission is broadly stated and includes living animals
The permission applies only to aquatic animals
The permission applies only to plants
challenge.explanation: The words “every” and “that liveth” present the permission broadly rather than limiting it to one kind of creature.

challenge.question: What does the comparison “even as the green herb” teach about permission to eat animals?
answers: Animals must eat grass
Living creatures were given as food just as plants were given as food
Human beings must be vegetarians
challenge.explanation: The verse compares giving animals as food with giving green plants as food, emphasizing permission to eat them.

challenge.question: To whom do the plural commands and pronouns, such as “be fruitful” and “you,” refer?
answers: Noah and his sons together
Noah alone
The animals alone
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly addresses Noah and his sons, so the plural language refers to all of them together.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the word “every” in the phrase “Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you”?
answers: The permission is broadly stated and includes living animals
The permission applies only to aquatic animals
The permission applies only to plants
questions.explanation: The words “every” and “that liveth” present the permission broadly rather than limiting it to one kind of creature.

questions.question: What does the comparison “even as the green herb” teach about permission to eat animals?
answers: Animals must eat grass
Living creatures were given as food just as plants were given as food
Human beings must be vegetarians
questions.explanation: The verse compares giving animals as food with giving green plants as food, emphasizing permission to eat them.

questions.question: To whom do the plural commands and pronouns, such as “be fruitful” and “you,” refer?
answers: Noah and his sons together
Noah alone
The animals alone
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly addresses Noah and his sons, so the plural language refers to all of them together.

paragraphs.title: The Sanctity of Blood and Responsibility for Human Life

easy.question: What must not be eaten according to verse 4?
answers: Flesh with its blood
Bread
Fruit
easy.explanation: The verse says that flesh with its life, which is its blood, must not be eaten.

easy.question: What will happen to one who sheds human blood?
answers: He will be expelled from the land
His blood will be shed
He will become wealthy
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed.”

easy.question: What does God command human beings to do in verse 7?
answers: Build a city
Protect the animals
Be fruitful, multiply, and fill the earth
easy.explanation: The verse commands them to be fruitful, multiply, and bring forth abundantly in the earth.

medium.question: Why is the punishment for shedding human blood so severe?
answers: Because human beings were made in God’s image
Because humans are stronger than all animals
Because humans live for a long time
medium.explanation: The verse explains the severity by saying, “For in the image of God made he man.”

medium.question: What is the main order of ideas in verses 4–7?
answers: Human multiplication, the prohibition of blood, then judgment on a murderer
The prohibition against consuming blood, responsibility for shedding blood, then the command to multiply
Judgment on a murderer, building an altar, then eating meat
medium.explanation: Verse 4 concerns blood in meat; verses 5–6 concern shedding human blood; and verse 7 commands people to multiply.

medium.question: In the phrase “your blood of your lives will I require,” what does “require” mean?
answers: I will bless
I will hide
I will demand an accounting
medium.explanation: In this context, requiring blood means demanding an accounting and punishing the shedding of blood.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the words “At the hand of every beast will I require it”?
answers: An animal that kills a person is also held accountable
All animals must be fruitful and multiply
People may not eat any animals
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the blood of a human being will also be required from an animal, so responsibility is not limited to humans.

challenge.question: What does “by man shall his blood be shed” mean in context?
answers: People may shed blood without judgment
The shedding of human blood will be answered by another human being
Only an animal may punish the murderer
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the punishment for shedding human blood will be carried out by a human being.

challenge.question: What connection is created between the prohibition against eating blood in verse 4 and the seriousness of shedding human blood in verses 5–6?
answers: Blood is ordinary food and has no special significance
Both prohibitions concern animals only
Blood is connected with life, so it must be treated with respect and human life must be especially protected
challenge.explanation: Verse 4 connects blood with life, while verses 5–6 emphasize the sacredness of human life made in God’s image.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the words “At the hand of every beast will I require it”?
answers: An animal that kills a person is also held accountable
All animals must be fruitful and multiply
People may not eat any animals
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the blood of a human being will also be required from an animal, so responsibility is not limited to humans.

questions.question: What does “by man shall his blood be shed” mean in context?
answers: People may shed blood without judgment
The shedding of human blood will be answered by another human being
Only an animal may punish the murderer
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the punishment for shedding human blood will be carried out by a human being.

questions.question: What connection is created between the prohibition against eating blood in verse 4 and the seriousness of shedding human blood in verses 5–6?
answers: Blood is ordinary food and has no special significance
Both prohibitions concern animals only
Blood is connected with life, so it must be treated with respect and human life must be especially protected
questions.explanation: Verse 4 connects blood with life, while verses 5–6 emphasize the sacredness of human life made in God’s image.

paragraphs.title: The Covenant with Noah, His Sons, and Every Living Creature

easy.question: To whom did God speak in these verses?
answers: Noah and his sons
Pharaoh and his servants
Adam and Eve
easy.explanation: The opening verse says that God spoke to Noah and his sons.

easy.question: What did God promise to establish with Noah?
answers: An altar
A covenant
A city
easy.explanation: God says, “I establish my covenant with you.”

easy.question: What would not happen again according to the passage?
answers: Famine in the land
The death of animals
A flood to destroy the earth
easy.explanation: God promises that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.

medium.question: Who besides Noah and his sons was included in the covenant?
answers: Only the people of the city
The living creatures that came out of the ark
Only Noah’s future descendants
medium.explanation: The verses also mention every living creature and the animals that came out of the ark.

medium.question: In the phrase “with your seed after you,” what does “seed” mean?
answers: The land belonging to Noah’s sons
Seeds planted in the ark
The descendants of Noah’s sons
medium.explanation: Here “seed” means descendants; “after you” shows that future generations are intended.

medium.question: What is the connection between the covenant and the promise in verse 11?
answers: The covenant includes a promise that there will never again be a destructive flood
The covenant commands Noah to build another ark
The covenant promises that all people will become kings
medium.explanation: The covenant is explained by the promise that all flesh will never again be destroyed by floodwaters.

challenge.question: Why do the verses specify birds, cattle, and beasts of the earth?
answers: To show that the covenant concerns the entire animal world that was with Noah
To command Noah to hunt all the animals
To distinguish ark animals from land animals only
challenge.explanation: The details emphasize that the promise is not limited to human beings but includes the animals as well.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the covenant was also made with “your seed after you”?
answers: The covenant was valid only while they were in the ark
The covenant was intended for generations not yet born
The covenant was made only with Noah’s sons and not with Noah
challenge.explanation: The words “after you” and “your seed” point to the continuation of the covenant in future generations.

challenge.question: What is the precise difference between the two parts of the promise in verse 11?
answers: The first concerns water, and the second concerns fire
The first concerns Noah’s sons, and the second concerns animals
The first promises that flesh will not be destroyed by floodwaters, and the second that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth
challenge.explanation: The verse uses two complementary expressions: there will be no destruction by floodwaters, and there will be no more destructive flood upon the earth.

questions.question: Why do the verses specify birds, cattle, and beasts of the earth?
answers: To show that the covenant concerns the entire animal world that was with Noah
To command Noah to hunt all the animals
To distinguish ark animals from land animals only
questions.explanation: The details emphasize that the promise is not limited to human beings but includes the animals as well.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the covenant was also made with “your seed after you”?
answers: The covenant was valid only while they were in the ark
The covenant was intended for generations not yet born
The covenant was made only with Noah’s sons and not with Noah
questions.explanation: The words “after you” and “your seed” point to the continuation of the covenant in future generations.

questions.question: What is the precise difference between the two parts of the promise in verse 11?
answers: The first concerns water, and the second concerns fire
The first concerns Noah’s sons, and the second concerns animals
The first promises that flesh will not be destroyed by floodwaters, and the second that there will never again be a flood to destroy the earth
questions.explanation: The verse uses two complementary expressions: there will be no destruction by floodwaters, and there will be no more destructive flood upon the earth.

paragraphs.title: The Rainbow as the Sign of the Everlasting Covenant

easy.question: What sign of the covenant is described in these verses?
answers: The rainbow
The cloud
The water
easy.explanation: The rainbow is the sign of the covenant between God, the earth, and every living creature.

easy.question: Where does the rainbow appear according to the passage?
answers: In the sea
In the cloud
On the mountain
easy.explanation: The verses say that the bow appears in the cloud when a cloud comes over the earth.

easy.question: With whom was the covenant in these verses made?
answers: With Noah alone
With the children of Israel alone
With every living creature and all flesh
easy.explanation: The covenant is between God and every living creature and all flesh upon the earth.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in these verses?
answers: A cloud appears, the rainbow is seen, and God remembers the covenant
The waters rise, the rainbow disappears, and then a covenant is made
Noah sees a rainbow, and then the flood begins
medium.explanation: When a cloud appears, the rainbow is seen, and God remembers the covenant and promises that there will be no more destructive flood.

medium.question: In the phrase “This is the token of the covenant,” what does “token” mean?
answers: Punishment
A sign
A story
medium.explanation: A token is a sign. Here, the rainbow is a visible sign of the covenant between God and the earth and its living creatures.

medium.question: What is the result of God remembering the covenant?
answers: The clouds always disappear
The rainbow turns into water
The waters will never again become a flood to destroy all flesh
medium.explanation: God remembers the covenant and therefore promises that the waters will never again become a destructive flood.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “between me and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth”?
answers: The covenant includes all living creatures on earth
The covenant belongs only to human beings
The covenant concerns only the land of Israel
challenge.explanation: The phrase “every living creature” broadens the covenant beyond Noah and shows that it concerns all living creatures on earth.

challenge.question: What does “for perpetual generations” mean in the context of the covenant?
answers: The covenant lasted only during Noah’s lifetime
The covenant was intended to continue through many generations forever
The covenant exists only when clouds appear
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the covenant is not temporary but is intended to continue through the generations.

challenge.question: According to the passage, what does the rainbow cause God to do?
answers: Create the earth again
Begin another flood
Remember the covenant
challenge.explanation: The verses repeatedly say that the rainbow serves as a reminder of the covenant, after which there will be no more destructive flood.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “between me and every living creature of all flesh that is upon the earth”?
answers: The covenant includes all living creatures on earth
The covenant belongs only to human beings
The covenant concerns only the land of Israel
questions.explanation: The phrase “every living creature” broadens the covenant beyond Noah and shows that it concerns all living creatures on earth.

questions.question: What does “for perpetual generations” mean in the context of the covenant?
answers: The covenant lasted only during Noah’s lifetime
The covenant was intended to continue through many generations forever
The covenant exists only when clouds appear
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the covenant is not temporary but is intended to continue through the generations.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does the rainbow cause God to do?
answers: Create the earth again
Begin another flood
Remember the covenant
questions.explanation: The verses repeatedly say that the rainbow serves as a reminder of the covenant, after which there will be no more destructive flood.

paragraphs.title: Noah’s Sons Leave the Ark and Spread across the Earth

easy.question: Who were Noah’s sons who came out of the ark?
answers: Shem, Ham, and Japheth
Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
Cain, Abel, and Seth
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly names Shem, Ham, and Japheth as Noah’s sons.

easy.question: Who was the father of Canaan?
answers: Shem
Ham
Japheth
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ham is the father of Canaan.”

easy.question: What happened to the whole earth through Noah’s sons?
answers: It remained empty
It was divided only among Noah’s sons
It was populated and spread out through them
easy.explanation: The verse says that the whole earth was overspread through Noah’s three sons.

medium.question: Why can Shem, Ham, and Japheth be called the beginning of the post-flood population?
answers: They were Noah’s sons who left the ark, and the whole earth was populated through them
They built the ark by themselves
They were the first three people in the world
medium.explanation: The verses connect their leaving the ark with the spread of humanity throughout the earth.

medium.question: In the phrase “of them was the whole earth overspread,” what does “overspread” mean?
answers: Was destroyed
Was spread out and populated
Was rebuilt
medium.explanation: The context shows that people spread out and populated the whole earth through these three sons.

medium.question: What logical order is described in the verses?
answers: The whole earth was populated, and afterward Noah’s sons left the ark
Ham fathered Canaan, and afterward the ark was built
Noah’s sons left the ark, and through them the whole earth was populated
medium.explanation: The passage first names Shem, Ham, and Japheth as those who left the ark, and then describes the spread of humanity through them.

challenge.question: What does the statement “These are the three sons of Noah” emphasize?
answers: That Noah had only three sons
That Ham alone was Noah’s son
That these three sons were the source through which the whole earth was populated
challenge.explanation: The statement summarizes the three names and connects them with the spread of humanity throughout the earth.

challenge.question: Which detail identifies Canaan specifically with Ham’s family rather than Shem’s or Japheth’s?
answers: The statement that Ham was Canaan’s father
The phrase “out of the ark”
The words “the whole earth”
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Ham was the father of Canaan, placing Canaan in Ham’s family.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “of them was the whole earth overspread”?
answers: All people remained together in one place
The spread throughout the earth is attributed to Noah’s three sons and their descendants
Only Canaan moved to another land
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the three sons named, through whom and their descendants humanity spread across the earth.

questions.question: What does the statement “These are the three sons of Noah” emphasize?
answers: That Noah had only three sons
That Ham alone was Noah’s son
That these three sons were the source through which the whole earth was populated
questions.explanation: The statement summarizes the three names and connects them with the spread of humanity throughout the earth.

questions.question: Which detail identifies Canaan specifically with Ham’s family rather than Shem’s or Japheth’s?
answers: The statement that Ham was Canaan’s father
The phrase “out of the ark”
The words “the whole earth”
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says that Ham was the father of Canaan, placing Canaan in Ham’s family.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “of them was the whole earth overspread”?
answers: All people remained together in one place
The spread throughout the earth is attributed to Noah’s three sons and their descendants
Only Canaan moved to another land
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the three sons named, through whom and their descendants humanity spread across the earth.

paragraphs.title: Noah’s Vineyard and His Sons’ Actions

easy.question: Who planted a vineyard?
answers: Noah
Shem
Ham
easy.explanation: The verse says that Noah planted a vineyard.

easy.question: What happened to Noah after he drank the wine?
answers: He left the tent
He became drunk
He planted a vineyard
easy.explanation: The verse says that Noah drank the wine, became drunk, and was uncovered inside his tent.

easy.question: Who covered their father’s nakedness?
answers: Ham and Canaan
Noah and Ham
Shem and Japheth
easy.explanation: Shem and Japheth took a garment and covered their father.

medium.question: What happened before Noah became drunk?
answers: Noah planted a vineyard
Shem and Japheth covered him
Ham told his brothers
medium.explanation: First Noah planted a vineyard; afterward he drank the wine and became drunk.

medium.question: What does the phrase “Noah began to be an husbandman” mean in context?
answers: A man who lived in the wilderness
A man who worked the land
A man who was made from the earth
medium.explanation: Since the verse says that Noah planted a vineyard, the phrase describes someone who worked in agriculture.

medium.question: Why did Shem and Japheth walk backward while covering Noah?
answers: To reach the tent quickly
Because they did not know where he was
So they would not see their father’s nakedness
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that their faces were turned backward so they would not see their father’s nakedness.

challenge.question: How does the verse describe the son whose actions Noah learned about after waking?
answers: His younger son
His older son
His wisest son
challenge.explanation: The verse explicitly calls him Noah’s younger son.

challenge.question: What is the main difference between Ham’s action and the action of Shem and Japheth?
answers: Ham slept, while they drank wine
Ham told others, while they covered their father
Ham covered his father, while they told others about him
challenge.explanation: Ham saw his father and told his two brothers, while Shem and Japheth covered their father without looking at him.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Noah “awoke from his wine” and only then learned what his son had done?
answers: Noah watched the entire event while drinking
Ham told Noah before he fell asleep
Noah discovered what happened after he became sober
challenge.explanation: The sequence shows that Noah learned what his son had done only after waking from his drunkenness.

questions.question: How does the verse describe the son whose actions Noah learned about after waking?
answers: His younger son
His older son
His wisest son
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly calls him Noah’s younger son.

questions.question: What is the main difference between Ham’s action and the action of Shem and Japheth?
answers: Ham slept, while they drank wine
Ham told others, while they covered their father
Ham covered his father, while they told others about him
questions.explanation: Ham saw his father and told his two brothers, while Shem and Japheth covered their father without looking at him.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Noah “awoke from his wine” and only then learned what his son had done?
answers: Noah watched the entire event while drinking
Ham told Noah before he fell asleep
Noah discovered what happened after he became sober
questions.explanation: The sequence shows that Noah learned what his son had done only after waking from his drunkenness.

paragraphs.title: Noah’s Words Concerning the Fate of His Sons

easy.question: Whom did Noah curse in verse 25?
answers: Canaan
Shem
Japheth
easy.explanation: Noah said, “Cursed be Canaan,” so Canaan is the one who was cursed.

easy.question: Who is called “the Lord God of Shem” in verse 26?
answers: Japheth
The Lord
Canaan
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem,” referring to the Lord.

easy.question: To whom was the statement “God shall enlarge Japheth” addressed?
answers: Shem
Canaan
Japheth
easy.explanation: Verse 27 explicitly says, “God shall enlarge Japheth.”

medium.question: What punishment for Canaan is repeated in verses 25–27?
answers: He would be a servant to his brothers
He would live in Japheth’s tents
He would be the God of Shem
medium.explanation: Canaan is called a servant of servants and is repeatedly described as a servant to others.

medium.question: What does “the tents of Shem” mean in context?
answers: Wars
Places of residence
Families
medium.explanation: Tents refers to dwellings or places of residence; “he shall dwell” confirms this meaning.

medium.question: What is the order of events in these verses?
answers: Japheth is enlarged, then Canaan is cursed, and finally Shem is blessed
Shem is blessed, then Japheth is enlarged, and finally Canaan is cursed
Canaan is cursed, then Shem is blessed, and finally Japheth is blessed
medium.explanation: Verse 25 presents Canaan’s curse, verse 26 blesses the Lord and refers to Shem, and verse 27 gives Japheth’s blessing.

challenge.question: According to the wording of verse 26, whom is the phrase “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem” blessing?
answers: The Lord, who is the God of Shem
Canaan
Japheth
challenge.explanation: The verse says “Blessed be the Lord,” so the blessing is directed to the Lord, who is then described as Shem’s God.

challenge.question: What special detail is added to Japheth’s blessing compared with Shem’s?
answers: Japheth will be Canaan’s servant
Japheth will dwell in the tents of Shem
Shem will dwell in Japheth’s tents
challenge.explanation: Japheth is not only promised enlargement but is also said to dwell in the tents of Shem.

challenge.question: What word connection stands out in the blessing of Japheth?
answers: The name Japheth is connected with becoming a servant
The name Japheth is connected with being the God of Shem
The name Japheth is connected with the idea of enlargement or expansion
challenge.explanation: The repeated use of “Japheth” and “enlarge” connects his name with the blessing that God would expand his territory or place.

questions.question: According to the wording of verse 26, whom is the phrase “Blessed be the Lord God of Shem” blessing?
answers: The Lord, who is the God of Shem
Canaan
Japheth
questions.explanation: The verse says “Blessed be the Lord,” so the blessing is directed to the Lord, who is then described as Shem’s God.

questions.question: What special detail is added to Japheth’s blessing compared with Shem’s?
answers: Japheth will be Canaan’s servant
Japheth will dwell in the tents of Shem
Shem will dwell in Japheth’s tents
questions.explanation: Japheth is not only promised enlargement but is also said to dwell in the tents of Shem.

questions.question: What word connection stands out in the blessing of Japheth?
answers: The name Japheth is connected with becoming a servant
The name Japheth is connected with being the God of Shem
The name Japheth is connected with the idea of enlargement or expansion
questions.explanation: The repeated use of “Japheth” and “enlarge” connects his name with the blessing that God would expand his territory or place.

easy.question: How many years did Noah live after the flood?
answers: 350 years
500 years
950 years
easy.explanation: The verse says that Noah lived 350 years after the flood.

easy.question: How many years did Noah live altogether?
answers: 350 years
950 years
600 years
easy.explanation: The verse says that all the days of Noah were 950 years.

easy.question: What happened to Noah at the end of his life?
answers: He left the ark
He was born
He died
easy.explanation: The end of verse 29 says, “And he died.”

medium.question: What does verse 29 add to what is said in verse 28?
answers: The total number of his years and his death
Only the number of years he spent in the ark
The names of his sons
medium.explanation: Verse 28 gives the 350 years after the flood; verse 29 adds Noah’s total lifespan and says that he died.

medium.question: In the phrase “Noah lived after the flood,” what does “after” mean?
answers: Before
Following
Inside
medium.explanation: “After” means following; the context refers to the years Noah lived once the flood had ended.

medium.question: Which sequence of events matches the verses?
answers: Noah died, then the flood came, and afterward he lived 350 years
Noah lived 950 years after the flood and then was born
The flood ended, Noah lived another 350 years, and then he died
medium.explanation: According to the verses, Noah lived 350 years after the flood and then died.

challenge.question: According to the numbers in these verses, how many years did Noah live before the flood?
answers: 600 years
350 years
950 years
challenge.explanation: If Noah lived 950 years in total and 350 years after the flood, he lived 600 years before the flood.

challenge.question: What does the word “all” emphasize in the phrase “all the days of Noah”?
answers: Only the years after the flood
The whole span of his life, from beginning to death
Only the years he spent in the ark
challenge.explanation: “All” makes clear that 950 years refers to Noah’s entire lifetime, not only the years after the flood.

challenge.question: Which statement accurately describes the numbers in the verses?
answers: Noah lived 350 years altogether
Noah lived 950 years after the flood
Noah lived 350 years after the flood and 950 years altogether
challenge.explanation: Verse 28 gives 350 years after the flood, while verse 29 gives 950 years for Noah’s entire life.

questions.question: According to the numbers in these verses, how many years did Noah live before the flood?
answers: 600 years
350 years
950 years
questions.explanation: If Noah lived 950 years in total and 350 years after the flood, he lived 600 years before the flood.

questions.question: What does the word “all” emphasize in the phrase “all the days of Noah”?
answers: Only the years after the flood
The whole span of his life, from beginning to death
Only the years he spent in the ark
questions.explanation: “All” makes clear that 950 years refers to Noah’s entire lifetime, not only the years after the flood.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes the numbers in the verses?
answers: Noah lived 350 years altogether
Noah lived 950 years after the flood
Noah lived 350 years after the flood and 950 years altogether
questions.explanation: Verse 28 gives 350 years after the flood, while verse 29 gives 950 years for Noah’s entire life.
